blocks.text: Breakpoints and watches are debugging tools that pause a program and let us examine its data at chosen points. They help find errors and show how the code flows, making debugging faster and more precise.

items: Breakpoint: a marker that pauses execution at a chosen line. In IDEs such as PyCharm or VS Code it is set by clicking in the margin next to the line number. When the program reaches it, execution stops and the current state (variable values) can be examined, so attention can go to one section of code.
Watch expression: tracks the value of a variable or expression while the program runs, updating automatically when the value changes, so unexpected values can be spotted step by step.
Step-by-step debugging: runs the code one line or function at a time to follow the program's logic and find exactly where an error occurs.

blocks.title: Example: a program to debug (Python code; each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
def calculate_area(radius):
....# Set a breakpoint here to check the value of radius
....area = 3.14 * radius ** 2
....return area

def main():
....# Step-by-step debugging starts here
....radius = 5
....print("Area of circle:", calculate_area(radius))
....radius = 10
....print("Area of circle:", calculate_area(radius))

if __name__ == "__main__":
....main()

items: calculate_area(radius) works out 3.14 * radius ** 2 and returns it; main() tests it with radius 5 and then 10.
Set breakpoints by clicking next to the lines radius = 5 and radius = 10; the program pauses there and the variables can be inspected.
Add a watch for radius to see it change from 5 to 10 as the program runs.
Step Into goes inside a function such as calculate_area(); Step Over runs the current line and moves to the next without going inside functions; Continue runs on to the next breakpoint.

blocks.alt: A code panel shows calculate_area and main with red breakpoint dots beside area = 3.14 * radius ** 2, radius = 5 and radius = 10; the area line is highlighted as the line where execution is paused. A watches panel shows radius = 5 and area = 78.5, and next run radius = 10, area = 314.0. Buttons Step Into (go inside calculate_area()), Step Over (run this line, go to next) and Continue (run to the next breakpoint) are explained.
blocks.caption: Breakpoints, watches and stepping in an IDE (original diagram after Fig 5.2).
blocks.long_description: Pausing at the area line and watching radius shows at once whether the function received the value expected; if not, the bug is in the caller, not in the formula.
